question_text: Which conduct is right?

options.text: The green car must wait
I may turn observing the traffic signs
I may only turn when the lights show "green"

correct_answers.text: The green car must wait
I may turn observing the traffic signs

comment: The traffic light system regulates the right of way for the traffic moving straight ahead. The turning lane on the left does not have its own traffic light. When turning left, you must therefore enter the intersection area and wait until a gap in the oncoming straight traffic allows you to pass. On the lane previously branching off for right-turning drivers, the traffic sign applies instead of the traffic light. Note the cross traffic when turning.

question_text: The traffic lights are on flashing amber. What is the correct procedure?

options.text: Approach with greater caution, giving way if necessary
Wait until the lights change

correct_answers.text: Approach with greater caution, giving way if necessary

comment: The yellow flashing light indicates that the traffic light is out of order. Instead, the traffic signs are valid that regulate the right of way and you must give priority here. Without traffic signs, the rule "left yields to right" applies.

question_text: What is permitted at these traffic lights with green arrow sign?

options.text: Turn right from the right lane after having stopped first, when there is no obstruction or danger to others
Turn right without stopping
Turn right only when the traffic lights are green

correct_answers.text: Turn right from the right lane after having stopped first, when there is no obstruction or danger to others

comment: The additional sign with green arrow on a black background allows you to turn right after stopping at the red traffic light. Despite the additional sign, the car driver has to make sure that the cross traffic is not endangered. This includes pedestrians and cyclists. Turning is permitted only on the right lane and may only be performed after stopping and ensuring that you can turn safely.

question_text: At these traffic lights with a green arrow sign, where should a vehicle stop before turning right?

options.text: At the stop line
Before the crossing or junction if there is no stop line
There is no need to stop

correct_answers.text: At the stop line
Before the crossing or junction if there is no stop line

comment: The car driver has to stop at the stop line. If none exists, then he has to stop in any case before the intersection or T-junction. If the traffic situation allows it, turning to the right is also possible when the traffic light is red. A right-turning driver should behave just as he does with a stop sign, when the traffic light is red. The right of way of the cross traffic must be considered and granted.

question_text: How should you behave in this situation?

options.text: Pass through the crossing without stopping
Stop on the line of sight
Stop on the stop line

correct_answers.text: Pass through the crossing without stopping

comment: The traffic light has priority over other traffic signs and lane markings. Cross the intersection without stopping, as long as the traffic light is green.

question_text: Where must you wait?

options.text: At the stop line
At the point where you can see along the intersecting road (sight line)
Level with the traffic lights

correct_answers.text: At the stop line

comment: A traffic light in operation has priority over traffic signs, which regulate the right of way. Also, if there is a stop line, stop there and wait until you are allowed to continue.

question_text: What is correct in this situation?

options.text: Traffic turning right may proceed
Traffic continuing ahead may proceed
Traffic turning left may proceed

correct_answers.text: Traffic turning right may proceed

comment: If a traffic light turns red, car drivers who want to drive straight ahead or to the left must stop and wait. If there is an additional traffic light with a glowing green arrow pointing to the right, it is allowed to continue driving and to turn right. A traffic light without additional traffic lights or arrows, however, is valid for all directions.

question_text: What should you do?

options.text: Continue driving
Slow down

correct_answers.text: Continue driving

comment: The traffic light switches from green to yellow directly in front of you. Your speed is 45 km/h. So, you're too fast in order to slow down and stop in front of the traffic light. There is also a truck behind you, which could hit you while doing an abrupt braking maneuver. Drive on briskly.

question_text: What is correct in this situation?

options.text: I may turn unimpeded
I must allow the oncoming traffic to pass through
I have to wait in the centre of the junction

correct_answers.text: I may turn unimpeded

comment: Basically, when turning left, you as a car driver have to grant the oncoming traffic right of way. Since in this situation, the green arrow lights on the opposite street corner, you can assume that the traffic light for the oncoming traffic is red. So, you can turn.

question_text: You want to turn right at these traffic lights with a green arrow sign. What is the right course of action?

options.text: I stop before the junction
I have to ensure that other road users are not impeded
I may turn right into any lane

correct_answers.text: I stop before the junction
I have to ensure that other road users are not impeded

comment: Thanks to the green arrow sign, you can turn at this traffic light even when it's red. To do this, merge right and come to a brief stop in front of the traffic light. Afterwards, make sure that you do not obstruct or endanger other road users. Also note that cross traffic still has priority.

question_text: What should you do?

options.text: Slow down
Continue driving

correct_answers.text: Slow down

comment: In front of you you see a traffic light changing from green to yellow. You drive at 40 km/h. Since you are still far enough from the traffic lights, you have to slow down.

question_text: What is the right course of action now?

options.text: I allow any cross traffic the right of way
I wait at the stop line for the next set of green lights
I drive through the junction quickly, because "yellow" is displayed

correct_answers.text: I allow any cross traffic the right of way

comment: If the yellow traffic light flashes, the traffic light system is out of operation. Then the general right of way applies. You are not on a priority road; therefore, possible cross traffic has the right of way.

question_text: Under what circumstances may you cross a junction during a red light?

options.text: To carefully afford space to an emergency vehicle with a blue flashing light and siren sounding
If there is a police officer on the junction directing traffic
Under no circumstances

correct_answers.text: To carefully afford space to an emergency vehicle with a blue flashing light and siren sounding
If there is a police officer on the junction directing traffic

comment: You are allowed to run over a red traffic light at an intersection under the following circumstances: If you want to carefully give way to an emergency vehicle with a blue flashing light and an emergency horn or if a police officer is regulating the traffic at the intersection.

question_text: You now want to turn right at these traffic lights with a green arrow sign. What is the right course of action?

options.text: I initially halt at the stop line
I ensure that other road users are not impeded
Without stopping, I take the turn at walking speed

correct_answers.text: I initially halt at the stop line
I ensure that other road users are not impeded

comment: If there is a green arrow sign at a traffic light, you are allowed to cross a red light if you have stopped at the stop line first. You may turn if there is no risk of obstructing or endangering other road users.

question_text:
What is the rule at this traffic-light-controlled junction with additional signage?
At this junction

options.text: - cyclists are permitted to turn right, even when the light is showing red
- motor vehicles are permitted to turn right, even when the light is showing red
- cyclists must turn right

correct_answers.text: - cyclists are permitted to turn right, even when the light is showing red

comment: On traffic lights with this additional sign, only cyclists, even at red, can turn to the right.

question_text: The traffic lights facing you have already been “green” for some time now. What is the right course of action now?

options.text: I continue driving, ready to brake because the traffic lights could change to “amber”
I watch the traffic lights closely
I accelerate to ensure that I can still safely pass through the junction while the traffic lights are “green”

correct_answers.text: I continue driving, ready to brake because the traffic lights could change to “amber”
I watch the traffic lights closely

comment: As the traffic light has been green for some time, there is a high probability that it will change to yellow at any moment. Keep driving, ready to brake, because you will have to stop if it switches to yellow. You must not speed up, as a maximum of 30 km/h is permitted.

question_text: You want to turn left and the lights are "green". On your left there is a tram wanting to proceed straight ahead. What is correct?

options.text: You must wait
The tram must wait
You must come to an agreement since there are no rules for this

correct_answers.text: You must wait

comment: Although you are allowed to drive, due to the green light, you have to grant the tram the right of way, as it continues straight ahead. You should therefore only enter the intersection halfway and let oncoming vehicles pass before turning left.

question_text: You have taken the right lane by mistake although you want to turn left. How are you allowed to proceed?

options.text: Straight ahead
To the right
To the left when the traffic lights are "green"

correct_answers.text: Straight ahead
To the right

comment: Due to the solid line, you must not change the lane here. Follow only the arrows on your lane. Turning left from this lane would be prohibited and would endanger or at least hinder other drivers.

question_text:
What is the right behaviour now?
I drive

options.text: - off now
- off only when the lorry drives on
- off only when my light is green

correct_answers.text: - off now

comment: Since this situation is a two-phase traffic light, there is no green signal. After the red light is off, you can catch up with the truck. If there was no space left behind the truck to the exit on the right, you would have to wait at the traffic lights until there was enough space to stop.

question_text: What is the right course of action now?

options.text: I allow any cross traffic the right of way
I wait at the stop line for the next set of green lights
I drive through the junction quickly, because "yellow" is displayed

correct_answers.text: I allow any cross traffic the right of way

comment: The traffic lights are out of order, therefore the right-of-way traffic signs apply. You must give way.
